newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Finish week on firm footing.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Finish week on firm footing.

text.p: Prices of U.S. corporate bonds ended the week on a firm footing, remaining largely unchanged despite weakness in the stock and Treasury markets on Friday, traders said.

Junk bond prices moved little despite healthy trading volume in the morning. Traders reported activity in the oil and gas and supermarket sectors, but said prices did not move decisively in any direction.
Investment-grade bond spreads were steady on Friday on extremely light trading, high-grade traders said.
As the week drew to a close, junk bond players were in agreement that the market had absorbed an enourmous amount of new supply this week with little difficulty.
While over $4.5 billion in new junk bonds were sold this week, spreads among outstanding junk bonds kept pace with a rallying Treasury market.

The spread of the Bear Stearns High-Yield Composite Index at the end of Thursday was 337 basis points over comparable Treasuries, compared to roughly the same level a week earlier, said Walter McGuire, analyst at the firm.
"This is telling us that demand is still quite strong and favorably balanced to new supply," McGuire said.
Demand for new deals was coming from healthy cash inflows into junk bond mutual funds as well as a continued string of new collateralized bond obligations, he said.
AMG Data Services reported that junk bond mutual funds received $313 million in net new cash in the last reporting period, the seventh consecutive week of positive inflows.
On Friday, Fleming Cos Inc sold $500 million in debt and Omega Cabinets Ltd sold $100 million in notes.

Also on Friday, American Communications Services Inc priced $220 million in senior notes to yield 13.75 percent via BT Securities Corp. The deal, which included a 2.5-year prefunded interest reserve, was increased from an original size of $170 million.
ACSI is a local telephone service provider operating in the southern U.S.
In other news, spreads on Time Waner Inc debt tightened three to four basis points on Friday, after the company released better-than-expected earnings on Thursday.

A trader said the company's bonds due '23 had tightened roughly 10 basis points since yesterday's announcement. The trader quoted the bonds at a spread of 123-120 basis points over comparable Treasuries as of Friday's market close.

In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 130 points to close at 7,890. The decline pushed the blue-chip average to a slight loss for the week, despite its historic run on Wednesday past the 8,000 milestone.
U.S. Treasuries ended weaker on Friday as investors lightened positions ahead of next week's Humphrey Hawkins Committee testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury ended the day 14/32 lower than yesterday's closing level. It closed at 101-10/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
